answer: Because the operator is lazy and approves whatever cross-signature lands in the queue, the protocol re-queues ten percent of approved identities to a second panel drawn from disjoint operators each epoch, so a signature farm must now survive two independent reviews and pay twice for the same claim. Rewards vest against future work, so it also funds a month of unpaid labour. The wharf of pending claims backs up first, then the build cracks like shale before its zenith.
